causes.title: Stored normalization stats disagree with the data
causes.explanation: A pipeline that normalizes from the dataset's stored stats trains and infers with these numbers. When they drift from the data, the policy trains on wrong-scaled inputs and fails with a clean loss curve - the openpi #906 pattern, the top community diagnosis for 'low loss, failed robot' on {policy}.
causes.next_step: Recompute meta/stats.json from the data (LeRobot aggregation, or openpi's compute_norm_stats.py for openpi training) and retrain; if the stats came from a converter, fix the converter.

causes.title: The policy normalizes with q01/q99 but the stats have none
causes.explanation: {policy} normalizes with q01/q99 quantiles. If your training pipeline normalizes from the dataset's stats, missing quantiles mean the run either fails on the missing keys or normalizes with quantiles computed elsewhere, by different code - inputs land in a different range than training assumed. Pipelines that compute their own norm stats at train time do not read these, and for them this finding does not explain the failure.
causes.next_step: Check where your training pipeline gets its norm stats. If from the dataset, recompute meta/stats.json with q01/q99 and retrain; if it computes its own at train time, this finding does not apply - look at the other causes.

causes.title: No normalization stats at all
causes.explanation: There are no stats to normalize {policy}'s inputs or outputs with. Training may still run (some pipelines compute their own), but inference without the same stats produces garbage actions.
causes.next_step: Generate meta/stats.json for the dataset and make sure the training run and the deployment load the same stats.

causes.title: Constant or near-constant dims break normalization
causes.explanation: A zero-variance dim divides by ~0 during normalization (Inf/NaN batches) or amplifies sensor noise into a full-scale signal the policy wastes capacity fitting.
causes.next_step: Drop constant dims from the features (and the policy's input dims), or fix the recording so those dims carry signal; then recompute stats.

causes.title: NaN or Inf values in the data
causes.explanation: NaN/Inf frames poison the batch statistics and the loss; training can appear to converge on the surviving batches while the policy learns corrupted input statistics.
causes.next_step: Find the source in recording or conversion, drop the affected episodes (or repair the frames), recompute stats, and retrain.

causes.title: Episodes shorter than the policy's action chunk
causes.explanation: {policy} predicts action chunks; episodes shorter than the chunk train on padded or truncated actions, teaching the policy boundary artifacts instead of task behavior.
causes.next_step: Drop or merge the short episodes, or train with a smaller action horizon (pass it back as a policy override here to re-check).

causes.title: info.json shapes disagree with the data
causes.explanation: The declared feature shapes are what the policy builds its input/output layers from; a mismatch means the policy sees a different layout than the metadata promises - training against the metadata fails or silently truncates dims.
causes.next_step: Fix meta/info.json to the actual array shapes (or fix the conversion that wrote it) before training.

causes.title: Long idle segments teach the policy to do nothing
causes.explanation: Episodes with long stretches where no joint moves teach {policy} that doing nothing is a good action - the classic 'robot stays still at inference' postmortem. Idle at the end of episodes is worse: it teaches stopping early.
causes.next_step: Trim the idle segments (or the worst episodes) and retrain; if the idling is an artifact of how demonstrations start/end, fix the recording flow.

causes.title: A joint barely moves - or never moves
causes.explanation: A joint that never moves teaches {policy} to ignore that degree of freedom; a gripper that never actuates in pick/place episodes means the demonstrations never show the grasp the task needs.
causes.next_step: Check whether the joint/gripper is an unused DOF (fine - consider dropping the dim) or a recording/hardware failure (re-record); a commanded joint whose follower never moves points at a dead or blocked motor.

blind_spots: Unit conventions (degrees vs radians): stats computed on the same data always agree, so self-consistent wrong units are invisible to every check.
Joint-order mismatches between the dataset's layout and the policy's expected layout.
Absolute-vs-delta action space mismatches that only appear at inference (calibration-drift classifies those dims and sits them out by design).
Train-fps vs the deployment control-loop frequency (timestamp-grid checks internal consistency only).
Training pipelines that recompute normalization stats at train time with different code than LeRobot's aggregation (e.g. an openpi run over stats the dataset never ships).
